what_this_closes.headline: THE VOUCHER OPERATOR SURFACE. scd registered POST /v1/vouchers/issue and NO CALLER EXISTED ANYWHERE -- no edged route, no Hotel Admin page, no CLI -- while the handler's own header claimed 'edged proxies to this route'. VOUCHER was therefore an authentication method a property could switch on, which then refused every guest, correctly, because there were no vouchers and no way to make one. This was the largest thing standing between the product and the Guest activation D41 defers.
what_this_closes.migration_0087: created_at and issued_by on iam_v2.vouchers (the table could say neither when a card was printed nor by whom); batch_id written for the first time since mg3 defined it, so a print run is addressable as a batch; the optional redemption window written for the first time -- internal/iamv2/repo_pg.go has always enforced [valid_from, valid_until) with NULL meaning unbounded, so EVERY voucher this system could issue was valid forever; the append-only voucher_code_reveals; and two SECURITY DEFINER kernels, voucher_revoke and voucher_code_generation_supersede.
what_this_closes.the_asymmetry_that_shaped_the_reveal: Both existing one-time-secret precedents -- the post-stay PIN and the guest-account password -- are HASHED, so 'shown once' is enforced by arithmetic and re-revealing is impossible. A voucher code is ENCRYPTED and RECOVERABLE. Single-use therefore cannot be enforced by the crypto and is not claimed to be: what makes a reveal safe is that it cannot happen UNSEEN. That is why the audit is a table with an append-only trigger rather than a log line, why the row and the recovery share one transaction, and why the dialog says who will see that you looked instead of promising this is the only time.
what_this_closes.rotation: iam_v2.voucher_code_key_generations has carried superseded_at since mg3; issuance reads it to find the ACTIVE generation and NOTHING had ever written it. Rotation was expressible in the schema and impossible in the product. It matters because a voucher pins the generation that indexed it: retiring one leaves every unredeemed card redeemable under the key it was sealed with while new codes are drawn under a fresh one -- something a single raw key could not express, because rotating it would invalidate every printed card in the building.
what_this_closes.three_permission_keys: vouchers (print, list, cancel) / voucher-codes (recover a code in the clear, under step-up and a bounded reason) / voucher-code-settings (the format, and key rotation). The `vouchers` row was NOT invented here: docs/ROLE_AND_SCOPE_MATRIX.md has stated it since long before the resource key existed, which is exactly why it was never enforced -- auth.go had no voucher key at all, so the documented boundary was decorative, and voucher_operator, the role NAMED for this capability, held no voucher permission whatsoever. The document is now binding: the same two tests that hold the guest-device row to the code run over all three voucher rows.
what_this_closes.why_the_second_key_is_not_redundant: Issuing already returns plaintext. Issuing creates codes NOBODY HOLDS YET; revealing reads a code somebody may already be carrying, possibly from a batch another operator printed. So a role with issue and no reveal genuinely cannot read another operator's batch. hotel_it_manager is that role deliberately: it owns configuration and the PMS integration, and neither job requires reading a guest's credential.

defects_this_increment_also_closed.dashboard_tiles: resources_site.go selected `status` from iam_v2.vouchers. The column is `state`, the value 'ISSUED' has never existed in iam_v2, and svc_edged holds no privilege on the table at all -- three independent reasons the query could never return anything, with the error swallowed by `_ =`, so both tiles read 0 permanently. The tiles now read scd's summary, and vouchers_active was renamed vouchers_redeemed because 'active' is a legacy voucher state iam_v2 does not have.
defects_this_increment_also_closed.a_form_nobody_could_complete: Issuance requires a package_revision_id, and package authoring lives behind the Phase-2 commerce admin flag while this surface deliberately does not. The form would have asked an operator to paste an identifier the product never displays. GET /vouchers/grantable lists the currently published revision of each package.
defects_this_increment_also_closed.documentation_describing_a_removed_produ: The config manual's voucher section described the LEGACY surface: 1-10000 cards, 6-10 characters, four character modes, a prefix, per-voucher plan changes. lib/api.ts carried orphan Voucher/VoucherBatch types with a `code` field a list must never hold. session-words.ts said 'the admin service cannot read voucher codes', which stopped being true the moment the audited reveal existed -- and an operator told a thing is impossible stops looking for the place it is possible.

my_own_error_this_increment: The first version of 0087 ended ALTER FUNCTION ... OWNER TO iam_v2_owner UNGUARDED. On a database with no such role that aborts the WHOLE migration, and because it is one transaction nothing applied at all -- the reveal table, the columns and the function rolled back silently. 0063 and 0067 already wrap the same statement; this had not copied them. AND THE VERIFICATION SCRIPT HID IT: its refused() helper treated any ERROR as a pass, so five constraint probes reported 'refused' for constraints that did not exist. That is the same mistake as reading bool_or over zero rows as 'no privilege' -- absence of the thing being tested looking exactly like the thing being tested passing. Both were fixed and the whole verification re-run clean.
evidence: Migration 0087 applied against the FULL numbered chain on a disposable PostgreSQL: the columns; the reveal table with no code-bearing column; UPDATE and DELETE on it refused by the append-only trigger; five CHECK refusals including an operator that does not exist; the revoke kernel moving UNUSED to REVOKED exactly once and refusing a second attempt, a missing operator, a short reason and a wrong site; rotation retiring a generation with who and why recorded, refusing a repeat; svc_scd holding no UPDATE on either vouchers or the generations table; the down direction removing everything while leaving the revoked voucher revoked; and the re-up restoring it. FAILED_NEW=0.
known_gap_stated_rather_than_closed: scripts/pmsd-pg-integration.sh applies a CURATED list of migrations ending at 0079, so 0080-0087 have no integration coverage in the gate. The DDL of 0084, 0085 and 0087 is verified against the full chain on a disposable PostgreSQL in this delivery's evidence, and factory-clean reconstruction proves both install paths agree -- but that is not gate-enforced per-run coverage. Extending the harness means tracing each added migration's dependencies through a hand-maintained list, and breaking it breaks the phase3 gate for every delivery. Recorded, not attempted here.
what_this_increment_did_not_do: NOTHING WAS DEPLOYED. No live database was written and no service was restarted. The voucher surface exists in the repository and not yet on the appliance.
go_live: NOT AUTHORISED and not performed. D41 remains in force; no real Guest activation.

the_review_round_and_what_it_found.summary: Five findings, all real. FOUR GATES WERE GREEN on the reviewed head; not one of these was a gate failure, which is the argument for the review existing at all.
the_review_round_and_what_it_found.a_voucher_granted_any_package_it_was_eli: THE ONE THAT MATTERS. iam_v2.vouchers.package_revision_id has been NOT NULL and pinned at issuance since mg3; the issuance path's comment says republishing a package must not change what an already-printed card is worth; and the screen this delivery added tells the operator 'What these cards grant'. NOTHING ENFORCED IT: iam_v2.auth_contexts carries voucher_id and no package pin, so a VOUCHER auth context reached ListEligiblePackages and CreateQuote with nothing to narrow it, and at a property with two voucher-eligible free tiers a card printed for the lower one could be redeemed against the higher. A claim made in two places and enforced in none is worse than no claim -- it is the reason nobody checks. Migration 0088 puts the invariant in p4_entitlement_grant_kernel for the same reasons 0084 put the burn there, before the subject lock and before any write; the offer path narrows too, so a guest is never shown the choice the kernel would refuse.
the_review_round_and_what_it_found.proved_in_both_directions: The printed tier is GRANTED and the card burns to REDEEMED; the other tier is REFUSED with the card still UNUSED, no entitlement row and the purchase still PENDING. My first fixture used a purchase trigger value the CHECK rejects, so the purchase row never existed and the run proved only the refusal -- a check that refused everything would have passed it. Half a proof presented as a proof is the same class of error as a probe that reads a missing object as a passing constraint, which this delivery had already made once. Fixture errors no longer go to /dev/null.
the_review_round_and_what_it_found.the_socket_was_not_the_boundary_it_was_a: Read off the appliance rather than assumed: /run/stayconnect/scd.sock is root:stayconnect 0660, and systemd reports User=stayconnect for BOTH edged and the network-facing portald. So portald could POST to the reveal route with any real operator UUID and receive a plaintext guest credential -- the step-up happens in edged and nothing proved it had happened. Under a shared uid no filesystem or group separation exists, and portald legitimately needs scd, so the two code-recovery routes now verify the peer's own identity (SO_PEERCRED + /proc/<pid>/exe, read at accept time) and FAIL CLOSED when the peer cannot be identified. WHAT IT IS NOT is written into the file: a process sharing the uid can ptrace edged, so this stops a mistake and not a compromise.
the_review_round_and_what_it_found.required_hardening_item_this_creates: SEPARATE THE SERVICE USERS. portald gets its own user and the scd socket group admits edged only. It is the real fix for the item above and it is a deployment change -- systemd User=, a new group, and verification that the guest portal still works -- so it belongs with the live increment rather than half-done here. Recorded in pre_live_operational_gaps.
the_review_round_and_what_it_found.three_narrower_findings: The grantable selector ignored p.active, so a package the property had deliberately withdrawn stayed printable. The card list requested no page, so after printing 500 cards 400 were absent and could be neither revealed nor cancelled; it now pages and states how many it is showing. And the settings request ran for payments_operator, which deliberately holds vouchers:read and no voucher-code-settings, so RBAC refused it and the panel said 'Loading...' forever -- read and write are now separate props and the panel is not rendered, rather than the role being widened to fix a rendering bug.
